clue.text: Man in church, intoxicated, quietly making a mess of rites

parts.note: intoxicated means high, as on drink or drugs
P stands for piano, the musical direction for playing quietly

indicators.note: making a mess of the word rites means jumbling its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunk churchman bungles the service while keeping his voice down.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior cleric, chief of the priesthood, is a man found in church.

clue.text: Hot tune from Sixties musical?

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hot, as on taps
an air is a melody or tune

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a catchy number from a show of the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: The rock musical famous for its hippie songs opened on Broadway in 1968, so it is a Sixties show.

clue.text: Person receiving conveyance from relative supporter

parts.note: a gran, or grandmother, is a relative
a golf tee supports the ball before it is struck

explanation.surface: A property transfer is made by a family member who backs the recipient.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a conveyance grants property, and the party to whom it is granted is its recipient.

clue.text: Poor reactions part creating delay

indicators.note: poor suggests the words reactions part are badly made and need putting into a new order

explanation.surface: Weak responses from one section of an audience hold things up.
explanation.definitionFit: To put things off or dawdle is to cause a delay in getting them done.

clue.text: I rave about educated girl ignoring a pest

indicators.note: about means the word for rave goes round the next piece

parts.note: to rave is to rant

indicators.note: ignoring the a means that letter is dropped from the girl's name

parts.note: Rita is the heroine of the play and film Educating Rita

explanation.surface: Someone complains loudly about a schooled young woman who pays no attention to an annoying person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'educated girl' points to Willy Russell's play Educating Rita; 'ignoring a' trims her name and 'about' wraps the rave word round what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: An irritant is something or someone that annoys, just as a pest does.

clue.text: Continue to be detained by house guests

indicators.note: to be detained by the words house guests means the letters sit inside that run of text

explanation.surface: A visitor is told to carry on staying, kept in by the people lodging there.
explanation.definitionFit: To segue is to move on smoothly without a break, continuing from one thing into the next.

clue.text: Lively horse loses right plate

indicators.note: lively suggests the remaining letters are jumped about into a new order
loses means a letter is taken away from the word horse

explanation.surface: A spirited racehorse throws one of its plates on the right side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses right' turns HORSE into HOSE; 'Lively' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: In racing a light horseshoe is called a plate, so the two words name the same thing.

clue.text: Criminal's cover left dump unprotected

parts.note: a hood is a head covering

indicators.note: unprotected means the word dump loses its outer letters, the protective shell

explanation.surface: A villain's disguise was left lying at an unguarded rubbish tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoodlum is a thug or gangster, a lawbreaker of the street kind.

clue.text: Point poor setter, say makes for financial security

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point

indicators.note: poor suggests the words setter say are badly put together and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A broke crossword compiler comments on what brings wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: Living on easy street is an idiom for being comfortably off with money worries gone.

clue.text: State of a house on the borders of Ireland

indicators.note: on, in an across clue, means the following pieces come after
the borders of Ireland are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone wonders about the condition of a home near the Irish frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: Morally justified in reforming this rogue?

indicators.note: reforming means the letters of this rogue are made over into a new shape

explanation.surface: A scoundrel turning over a new leaf might feel virtuous about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Righteous means acting in a way that is morally right and defensible.

clue.text: Establishment offering ecstasy in food?

parts.note: transport can mean rapture or ecstasy, and a café offers food, so a roadside eatery reads as a place serving bliss

explanation.surface: A restaurant promises delight with every dish.
explanation.walkthrough: A transport café is a British roadside diner for lorry drivers; the clue plays on transport meaning rapture.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheap roadside eating place for truckers is a food establishment whose first word can mean ecstasy.

clue.text: Gain upper hand, seeing article covered by Spinners

indicators.note: covered by means the article sits inside the word for spinners

parts.note: turntables are record decks that spin
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A team wins the advantage when a news story is reported by the Spinners.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn the tables is an idiom for reversing a situation to get the advantage over a rival.

clue.text: Accommodation for a section with workers on empty trains

parts.note: a part is a section
men are workers, as in a firm's staff

indicators.note: empty means the word trains loses its insides, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: Seating is found for a group of employees on carriages with nobody aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Apartments are a set of rooms to live in, a form of lodging.

clue.text: Letting on perhaps, initially to be agreeable

indicators.note: on means the letting word comes after the initial letter in this across answer
initially means take the first letter of perhaps

parts.note: letting a property is leasing it

explanation.surface: A landlord wonders whether renting out a flat may begin as something pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pleasing gives satisfaction, so it is agreeable.

clue.text: A few locked in centre of firm's compound

indicators.note: locked in means the few go inside the centre letters
centre of means the middle letters of firm

parts.note: a few means some

explanation.surface: Several people are shut inside the heart of a company's premises.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry an isomer is a compound with the same atoms as another but a different arrangement.

clue.text: Credit America, turning up communist campaigner

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
USA, the United States of America

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a red is a communist

explanation.surface: Praise for the United States as a Marxist activist appears.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusader is someone who campaigns energetically for a cause.

clue.text: Radio broadcast key for member of crew

indicators.note: broadcast suggests scattering, so the letters of radio are spread into a new order

parts.note: E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A radio transmission is key for one of the team.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadie is one of the road crew who set up a touring band's equipment.

clue.text: A sailor reported following second attack

indicators.note: following means the sailor piece comes after the second
reported means the word is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a salt is an old sailor

explanation.surface: A mariner is said to come after a brief moment.
explanation.walkthrough: SAULT is pronounced like salt, the slang for an old seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: An assault is a violent attack on someone.

clue.text: Preserve wood in Greek island full of love like this

indicators.note: full of means the island holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: Crete is the largest Greek island
O is love, a nil score in tennis
so means like this, in this way

explanation.surface: Timber is kept on a Greek island that is full of romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Creosote is a tar oil painted onto fences and timber to stop rot, so to apply it preserves wood.

clue.text: Show respect for see

definitions.meaning: to keep or honour a rule or custom, as with a holiday

explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both honouring a custom and noticing with the eyes.

clue.text: State hates cuts planned in service

indicators.note: in means the reworked letters go inside the service

parts.note: Mass is a church service

indicators.note: planned means the letters of hates cuts are rearranged to a design

explanation.surface: A government detests spending reductions that are drawn up in its department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planned' rearranges the fodder, and 'in' sets it between the last two letters of the service word, not at its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Massachusetts is one of the states of the USA.

clue.text: Minor difficulty with answer for one to concoct

indicators.note: for means the answer letter takes the place of one

parts.note: a hitch is a small snag
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A small snag has a solution for someone to dream up.
explanation.definitionFit: To hatch a plan is to devise or contrive it.

clue.text: Love of French son's poetic output

parts.note: O is love, a nil score in tennis
de is French for of
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A French boy's affection is shown in the verses he writes.
explanation.definitionFit: Odes are lyric poems, the work a poet produces.

clue.text: Feeling queasy, dean arranged to accept university chair

indicators.note: to accept means the rearranged letters take the other pieces inside
arranged means the letters of dean are put in a new order

parts.note: a chair is a seat

explanation.surface: A college dean feels sick after being given a professorship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' scrambles the dean, and 'to accept' splits it after its second letter to take the university and the chair.
explanation.definitionFit: Nauseated means made to feel sick, which is being queasy.

clue.text: Bitter and cold — dry outside

indicators.note: outside means the dry word sits around the cold letter

parts.note: arid means very dry

explanation.surface: A drink is sharp, chilled, and parched to the edges.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrid taste or smell is harsh and sharp, so it is bitter.

clue.text: What wet concrete does for tennis?

definitions.meaning: a tennis match is divided into scoring units of games

explanation.surface: Someone asks what happens to fresh cement when it comes to a sports match.
explanation.definitionFit: Concrete hardens as it dries, and a tennis match is played over several such units.

clue.text: They'll give an edge for writer accommodated by flatmates

indicators.note: accommodated by means the writer is housed inside the flatmates word

parts.note: flatmates are sharers of a flat
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A writer is put up by the people sharing a flat to gain an advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharpeners hone knives or pencils, giving them a keen cutting edge.
